evidence.observation: The plan says `constraint_requirements` handles family `anchored` like `textual`: it appends a row to `model.unchecked` and returns no requirement, and says the DuckDB program then exits 4. In this checkout, `checker/_core.py` `_vacuity_message` and `semantic_spec.py` `applicability_of` classify an anchored rule whose subject fact type is empty as vacuous before the unchecked-anchor branch. The proposed static row would instead print not checked and exit 4 on that accepted population.

concerns.recommendation: Make the anchored report depend on the subject fact list at runtime, and add an empty-subject oracle case that compares findings and exit codes with `gnd check`.
concerns.title: Anchored rules are vacuous when their subject is empty

evidence.observation: The plan says a disconnected or ambiguous join `is listed as not checked through RP2's mechanism` and tests exit 4. In `semantic_spec.py:2895–2933`, empty-subject vacuity precedes `join_refusal_of`; `checker/_core.py` likewise handles an all-empty subject scope before join evaluation. With every referenced fact list empty, GND reports vacuous, while the proposed model-level `UNCHECKED` row would report not checked.

concerns.recommendation: Preserve GND's vacuity-before-join-refusal order in the generated report, and test disconnected and ambiguous joins with all referenced fact lists empty.
concerns.title: Static join refusals override GND's empty-subject verdict

evidence.observation: D6 says to refuse large integers `in a Number or Float role`; §2 places the guard in `check_cell`. Model-side constants also enter Float relations: `pyrel_rules.py` `_allowed` emits `allowed` values into a Float-typed helper without a bound check. For an allowed Number value of 9007199254740993 and a population role value of 9007199254740992, the role passes D6, while the model constant cannot be represented exactly as Float. GND's `values.py` retains their distinct integer ratios.

concerns.recommendation: Apply the exactness rule to model-side numeric literals and bounds before export, or use an exact lowering; add an oracle case with a large allowed value and a representable neighboring input.
concerns.title: D6 guards population cells but leaves model constants inexact

response.summary: Reviewed the inline r3 plan bytes only: this seat was instructed not to call a filesystem or shell tool, so the plan's src/gnd and tests line citations were not independently verified, and every concern below is an internal defect visible in the plan text itself. Several (p1) repairs hold as written: same-verdict scoped to accepted inputs with named exit-3 refusals, D6, the RP2-before-RP1 ordering in §3 and §9, the comparator extension with negative control RP2-C6, and the Ossie tests added to every phase lane. Three concerns are blocking: line :882 is cited both as the external-uniqueness refusal RP1 lifts and as an external-frequency refusal RP1 keeps; RP2-C4 and §5 promise a byte-identical textual report line while §10 requires the LQP program to gain textual not-checked lines; and RP2-C7 executes generated LQP code in the default lane, which §0 forbids and §8's venv split suggests the default environment cannot import. The remaining concerns are hardening gaps where a refusal or a divergence from GND is asserted without measurement, or where a §4 criterion names no lane that can discharge it.

The RP1 lowering mirrors _join_rows (anchor matching keyed by object type, vacuity on empty join, disconnected/ambiguous joins listed not checked via semantic_spec's classification, rendered unchecked at _core.py:569-577); D1/D2/D4/D5/D6 agree with checker behavior once §0's accepted-inputs scoping and exit-3 by-name refusals are applied, and none can make an accepted input disagree with gnd check. Round-1 repairs (per evidence/plan-review-r1/disposition.md) all hold against the code: the comparator gap (:62-73 json-decodes the reason; :83-102 drops unchecked-with-no-facts) is closed by RP2-C6 before any criterion relies on it; RP2-C4 pins the textual line byte-identical against :1648; D6 covers the exact-ratio gap (values.py:392-399) for Float as well as Number; the Ossie risk is bounded (uniqueness is not in _SUPPORTED at ossie_formulas.py:40-42, and fact-scoped value/D4 paths are bound by the §0 rule plus per-lane Ossie tests); phase order RP2,RP1,RP3,RP4,RP5 is consistent across sections 3, 8 and 9, and the draft RP1 spec is consistent with the plan. No blocking, hardening or completeness concerns found.

evidence.location: section 1, 'Populations for the agreement criteria' table, resolution row (line 127)
evidence.observation: The row reads: '| `resolution/model.orm.yaml` | the 80 `resolution/cases/*/*/population.json` | 4 (first case measured; the rest are measured by the RP5 test itself) |'. At this checkout `find src/gnd/examples/literature/resolution/cases -name population.json` returns 41 files (20 case directories, 41 whale subdirectories, each population.json sitting beside a population.json.anchors.json sidecar); no glob over that tree yields 80. The table is prefaced 'Measured on 2026-11-21', and RP5-C2 (line 317) keys off it: 'on each population named in §1's population table `(p1)`, the DuckDB program agrees with GND, with the GND exit that table records'.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the count to the measured number (41) and re-derive the other rows' counts the same way before the RP5 spec sizes its parameterisation from this table; the criterion itself stays testable either way, since it iterates the glob rather than the stated count.
concerns.title: Section 1's measured population table miscounts the resolution cases: 80 claimed, 41 exist

evidence.location: section 9, lanes table, RP1 row (line 398) and RP3-RP5 rows (lines 399-401)
evidence.observation: The RP1 row makes cumulativity explicit: 'the same with `tests/test_rp1_external_uniqueness.py` in place of the RP2 file, plus `tests/test_rp2_anchored.py`'. The later rows say only 'the same with `tests/test_rp3_number.py` added', 'the same with `tests/test_rp4_role_value.py` added', 'the same with `tests/test_rp5_literature_rules.py` added', which most naturally read as the RP2 row's list plus one file: on that reading RP3's lane never runs test_rp1_external_uniqueness.py, RP4's never runs the RP1 or RP3 files, and no listed default or oracle lane ever runs the rp1, rp3 and rp4 files together — although section 3 (line 292) has all four phases editing `pyrel_rules.py` one after another, 'one at a time on one branch'.

concerns.recommendation: State in section 9 that each phase's lane includes every earlier phase's new test file (or add one final lane that runs all five files together), so a regression a later phase introduces in an earlier phase's construct is caught by a listed lane and not only by RP5-C1/C2's packaged-model sweep.
concerns.title: Section 9's RP3-RP5 lanes are not unambiguously cumulative over earlier phases' test files

evidence.location: section 0, 'Ossie export unchanged' bullet (lines 72-79) and section 6 risk row (line 349)
evidence.observation: The binding rule's stated tripwire is 'Its committed tests (`tests/test_ossie_formulas.py`, `tests/test_ossie_export.py`) run in every phase's lane' and the risk row's control is 'the Ossie tests run in every phase's lane; §0'. tests/test_ossie_formulas.py (13 tests) contains no value-family case at all (no match for 'value', 'role_ref', or a fact-scoped value constraint). Yet the phases open exactly those shapes through the shared lowering ossie_formulas.py:293 calls: RP3 puts `Number` in `_TYPES`, so a value constraint over a Number-typed object type stops raising ExportInputError (today caught at :295 as 'not projected') and can newly project, and D4's `String` makes `raw_primitive` resolve an external-mode entity — the residual case _core.py:1275-1278 exists to admit. Round 1's disposition row 8 (evidence/plan-review-r1/disposition.md) names this shared path as 'partly' reached and cites this repair as the fix.

concerns.recommendation: Have the RP3 and RP4 specs add an Ossie-side pin for the shapes each phase newly makes lowerable (a projection-unchanged test, or an explicit keep-refusing guard in the Ossie path), rather than resting section 0's binding rule on committed tests that cover none of them.
concerns.title: The committed Ossie tests named as the section 0 backstop cover none of the shapes RP3/RP4 newly make lowerable

evidence.observation: Plan section 3 fixes the homes: 'review fixtures in `tests/fixtures/pyrel-rules-families/review/`', and section 9 adds '(p1) Every focused lane below also runs `tests/test_ossie_formulas.py tests/test_ossie_export.py`'. The RP1 draft spec (notes/phase-RP1-spec.md), which presents itself as 'amended for plan r3 `(p1)`' (spec line 5), diverges on both: its section 8 puts fixtures 'under `tests/fixtures/pyrel-rules-coverage/rp1/`' (spec line 150), and its verification ledger's focused lane is 'tests/test_rp1_external_uniqueness.py tests/test_pyrel_rules.py tests/test_pyrel_rules_families.py tests/test_pyrel_export.py tests/test_pyrel_export_boundaries.py' with no Ossie file and no test_rp2_anchored.py (spec line 172) — the (p1) lane widening is not reflected in the phase that runs first.

concerns.recommendation: When the RP1 spec is finalised at its gate, align its fixture home and verification ledger with plan sections 3 and 9 (or record the divergence as a spec ruling), so the round-1 lane and Ossie repairs are not silently dropped where they first execute.
concerns.title: The RP1 draft spec's fixture home and focused lane diverge from plan sections 3 and 9

response.summary: Verified the artifact's sha256 and read every citation against the repository (src/ and tests/ are byte-identical to the cited 8c909013): all code, test, doc and schema line references matched, including pyrel_rules.py 187/190/596/686-699/745/845-886/1257/1584-1585/1647-1649/2057-2126/2461-2466/2532-2533/2545, checker/_core.py 569-577/893-899/983-986/1099-1156/1275-1278/2071-2074, semantic_spec.py 2583-2593/2665-2672/2696-2700/3064-3065, ossie_formulas.py 272/293/295, checking.py 890-891, values.py 392-399, pyrel_runtime.py 172, tests/test_pyrel_rules.py 62-73/83-102/106-127/277/290-293, families :98, docs/runtimes/pyrel.md:156-161, rules-as-pyrel.md:69-70, representation-format.md 9/76/1309, and the fixture models and populations (12 gold populations; the interop anchored constraint arrives via the vocabulary include). The RP1 two-copy join mirrors _join_rows (anchors keyed by object type, per-copy variables, 'same' over anchor pairs) and its GND-side claims about vacuity, unchecked joins, external-mode typing and exit bands all match the checker. Every (p1) repair from round 1 holds: the comparator gap is real and RP2-C6 fixes it before use, D4/D6 refusals are scoped to inputs the program cannot represent exactly with both exits pinned, the textual line stays byte-identical, and the Ossie rule now names the shared-lowering path. Four non-blocking concerns: a miscounted population glob in section 1's measured table; section 9 lanes that are not unambiguously cumulative across phases; the committed Ossie tests named as the section 0 backstop cover none of the shapes RP3/RP4 newly make lowerable; and two divergences between the plan and the RP1 draft spec.

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented or tested as written, or the milestone would not do what its goal claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
Can each phase RP1 to RP5 be specified, implemented and tested as sections 2 and 4 write it, within the scope of sections 1 and 7? Is any criterion in section 4 impossible or unfalsifiable?

Does each code location, line number, quoted message and measured GND behaviour cited in the plan (especially section 1) match the repository at this checkout? Read the cited lines in src/gnd and tests before reporting a mismatch.

Do the binding rules of section 0 (including same-verdict scoped to accepted inputs, and Ossie export unchanged) and the proposals of section 10 (D1, D2, D4, D5, D6) agree with what GND's checker actually does, and with the criteria? Would any of them make the DuckDB program disagree with gnd check on an input it accepts?

Is the external-uniqueness lowering of section 2 RP1 the same join GND's checker uses (src/gnd/checker/_core.py _join_rows; semantic_spec.py join classification), including vacuity, ambiguous and disconnected joins, and anchor matching by object type?
Are the order, dependencies and verification lanes of sections 3, 8 and 9 consistent and sufficient for each criterion, including the opted-in pyrel_oracle lane?
Round 1's findings and their dispositions are in evidence/plan-review-r1/disposition.md; r3's repairs are tagged (p1). Judge whether each repair holds, and whether a repair introduced a new defect.

The RP1 draft spec at .gnd-planning/milestones/pyrel-rules-coverage/notes/phase-RP1-spec.md may be read for context; a concern about it must still cite the plan file and name the spec line in the observation.
Every concern's evidence must cite the plan file.
